fields.meta_title: Makeup Quiz: Find Your Everyday Look or Build One | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a free makeup quiz that names your everyday look in eight questions, then build one for a beauty brand, a bridal artist, or a class.
fields.h1: Build a Makeup Quiz for Beauty Brands and Makeup Artists
fields.hero_description: Build a makeup quiz that matches a look or a foundation shade, or take the eight-question one below to find your everyday look.
fields.features_heading: How a Makeup Quiz on Emergent Works
fields.features_subheading: A makeup quiz turns answers about routine, finish, and skin into one look or shade. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Match a look or score a test

Choose how answers count. In a look finder, every option points to one of your looks. In a class quiz, one option per question is correct, and the result is a total score.
fields.feature_2:
Shades listed on the result screen

Tag foundation, blush, and lip shades to each look in a product table. The result screen lists the shades tagged to that look, and a retagged shade shows up on the next result.
fields.feature_3:
One row for every finished quiz

The look, each option picked, and an email when someone offers one are saved as a row in a database you own. Filter for the Bold look and read what those shoppers chose first.
fields.feature_4:
Sized for a thumb on a phone

Emergent builds the quiz as a conversational flow with one question per screen. Someone tapping in from a video link answers all eight without zooming in or scrolling sideways.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when a result needs an artist

Send an email or Slack alert when a result needs a person, such as a bride booking her makeup trial. The alert names her look and links to each answer she gave in the quiz.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and your code on paid plans

Host the quiz on your brand's own domain: custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Beauty Businesses Run a Makeup Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
From two answers, a match on shade W32

Ines Hallam opens the shade finder on Verbena Row Cosmetics' site. She says the veins on her wrist look green and picks medium coverage. Her result screen shows foundation shade W32 from the brand's warm range, and her result and email are saved to the customer table.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every bride's result lands 7 days before her trial

Petra Vance books bridal makeup trials and sends the makeup quiz with each booking confirmation. Seven days before a trial, the app emails Petra the bride's look and answers. Maren Quist landed on Glam and asked for no strip lashes. Petra packed individual lashes for her Saturday trial.
fields.tab_content_3:
Color correcting, missed by 11 students in 18

Joelle Marchetti teaches a Saturday makeup course and gives her 18 students a ten-question quiz after the color theory lesson. The app scores every answer against her answer key. Question 6, on color correcting, was missed by 11 of 18, and she reteaches it next Saturday.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 1,040 Glam results, a four-part series

Harriet Ennis films makeup tutorials and links her makeup quiz from every video. In March, 2,600 viewers finished it. Glam led with 1,040, ahead of Classic at 820, Natural at 460, and Bold at 280. Her next four videos are a Glam series.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Makeup Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a makeup quiz that gives each person one look or one shade and keeps the answers behind it.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the quiz is for
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add an undertone question for shades
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick one job before writing a question. A look finder sorts people into looks, and a shade finder points each shopper to one foundation shade. A class quiz scores what students know instead. Put the job in your first prompt to Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the results before the questions: four looks such as Natural, Classic, Glam, and Bold, each with two lines on what sets it apart. The questions get easier once you know what they have to separate. Four results keep eight questions enough.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people do on an ordinary morning: how many minutes makeup takes and which finish they reach for. Habits separate looks better than asking which photo someone likes. Give every question one option per look, worded in plain shopper terms.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For a shade finder, ask about wrist veins. L'Oreal Paris says blue or purple veins suggest a cool undertone and greenish veins a warm one, and seeing both points to neutral. Pair it with a coverage question to land on one shade.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Say where to check the match
fields.howto_step_5_des: Under the shade on the result screen, add one line on checking it. The same L'Oreal Paris guide says to test shades on your jawline or just below it, in natural daylight, because store lighting often distorts undertones.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with four real faces
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, have four people take the quiz, one you expect to land in each look. When someone lands somewhere unexpected, reword the question that separated the two looks least. Then run all four through again before you share the link.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the counts after a month
fields.howto_step_7_des: After a month, open the results table and set the count for each look beside your stock or lesson plan. Drop any question that every person answers the same way, since it separates nothing. Rename a look nobody lands on.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a makeup quiz for my cosmetics brand that matches shoppers to one of four looks and shows the shades for each.

faq_plan.a: It is an eight-question quiz on this page that sorts your answers into one of four everyday looks: Natural, Classic, Glam, or Bold. The questions cover your morning routine and the finish you like, and each result suggests a place to start with shades.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a makeup quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz to Emergent's AI survey builder: the looks or shades you want as results, the number of questions, and what each finished quiz should save. Emergent builds the questions, the result screens, and the database behind them. Change any question later by prompt, then publish the quiz on your own site.

faq_plan.q: How do I find my makeup style quiz?
faq_plan.ref: How do I find my makeup style quiz?

prov.original: How do I find my makeup style quiz?

faq_plan.a: Take the eight questions on this page and your result names the look your answers lean toward. Answer for an ordinary weekday instead of a wedding or a night out, because an event pulls every answer toward Glam and hides what you wear most.

faq_plan.q: Can I build a free makeup quiz for my beauty brand?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. A free makeup quiz for shoppers is a sensible first build: there are no response caps, and every finished quiz still counts during a busy launch week.

faq_plan.q: Which makeup quiz questions help match a foundation shade?
faq_plan.a: Pair an undertone question with a coverage question, then map each pair of answers to one shade. Ask about undertone first: e.l.f. Cosmetics notes that a warm-toned foundation may turn orange on cool skin, while a cool-toned one might look too gray on warm skin. The coverage answer then picks between a sheer and a fuller formula in that undertone.

faq_plan.q: How do I write makeup quiz questions and answers for a class?
faq_plan.a: Write one question per skill you taught, with one correct answer and three wrong ones that sound as likely and run the same length. Add a one-line explanation under each one. A student who misses it then learns why. The app Emergent builds keeps every student's answers in a database you own, ready to count misses by question.

faq_plan.q: When is a makeup quiz better than a shade chart?
faq_plan.a: A quiz works better when shoppers cannot read their own undertone from a row of swatches on a screen. It asks two or three things they can check at home and names one shade. With a small range, say six shades, a chart that shows each one on several skin tones can do the job alone.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a makeup quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for six to ten. The quiz on this page uses eight, with one option per look in every question. That gives each look eight chances to score. Stop adding questions once your test group lands where you expected, since each extra screen is one more place to quit.

faq_plan.q: Should a makeup quiz ask for an email before the result?
faq_plan.a: No. Show the result first, then offer the shades by email. Someone who has just seen their look has a reason to type an address, and a gate before the result reads like a toll. Keep the field optional and say in one line what you will send.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a makeup quiz work for people who wear little makeup?
faq_plan.a: Write the Natural result so it fits someone whose routine is tinted moisturizer and lip balm, or nothing at all. Include an option like 'under five minutes, or I skip it' in the routine question. In the flow Emergent builds, each question gets its own screen, and a quick answer takes one tap.

quiz.title: What Is Your Everyday Makeup Look?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about your routine, your finish, and where you wear makeup. Your result names the look your answers lean toward, with products to start from.

questions.text: How long does your makeup take on an ordinary weekday morning?

options.text: Under five minutes, or I skip it
About ten minutes
Twenty minutes or so
As long as the look needs

questions.text: Which finish do you reach for on your skin?

options.text: Bare skin or a tinted moisturizer
A satin foundation that looks even
A glowy base with highlighter
Matte coverage that lasts all day

questions.text: What do you do with your eyes most days?

options.text: Nothing, or a clear brow gel
A neutral shadow and one coat of mascara
Blended shimmer and lashes that stand out
A sharp liner wing or a bright color

questions.text: Which lip do you wear most?

options.text: Lip balm
A nude or rosy lipstick
A glossy pink or mauve
A red, berry, or deep plum

questions.text: Where do you wear makeup most often?

options.text: On weekends, if at all
At the office and in meetings
At dinners and evenings out
At shows, parties, and photo shoots

questions.text: A friend compliments your makeup. What did they most likely notice?

options.text: That you look rested
That you look put together
That your skin looks lit from within
Your lip or eye color

questions.text: How many makeup products do you use in a normal week?

options.text: Fewer than five
A small set I repeat every day
A full kit with a few palettes
Lots of colors I rotate through

questions.text: What would you most like to learn next?

options.text: A two-minute routine that looks like skin
A neutral eye that works for work
A soft smoky eye for evenings
A graphic liner or a bold lip

results.title: Natural
results.description: Your answers lean toward skin that looks like skin. Start with a tinted moisturizer, a brow gel, and a tinted lip balm, and keep the whole routine under five minutes.

results.title: Classic
results.description: Your answers lean toward a polished look that holds up through a workday. Start with a satin foundation, a neutral eyeshadow, one coat of mascara, and a rosy lipstick.

results.title: Glam
results.description: Your answers lean toward a soft, glowing look for evenings and plans. Start with a glowy base, a highlighter, a blended shimmer shadow, and a glossy pink or mauve lip.

results.title: Bold
results.description: Your answers lean toward color and contrast. Start with a long-wear matte base, a sharp liner or a bright shadow, and a red or berry lip, and let one feature lead.

plan.angle: The top 10 is beauty brands' shade finders and routine quizzes plus BuzzFeed-style fun quizzes, with one quiz builder (Interact). A visitor can take an eight-question makeup quiz on this page that names their everyday look, then see four ways a beauty business runs one: a cosmetics brand matches a foundation shade from an undertone question, a bridal makeup artist reads each bride's result before the trial, a makeup teacher scores a ten-question class quiz and reteaches the most-missed question, and a makeup creator picks her next tutorial series from the result counts. The how-to covers results, undertone questions sourced to a cosmetics brand's guide, and testing; the FAQ covers free builds, question writing, answer keys for a class, and length.
